title: MyLinden prescription terms: replacing lost, stolen or damaged medication
content:
**Replacement of lost or stolen medication — Prescriptions & Renewals terms.**

(1) Where the class of the prescription allows lost or stolen replacement, one replacement fill may be authorized for medication that was lost or stolen, when the replacement fills authorized on that prescription in the rolling 12 calendar months ending on the day of handling are below the class's yearly replacement cap.

(2) The replacement is posted on the prescription's fill ledger as an authorization with reason "replacement fill" and one fill.

(3) Where the class requires a police report for a stolen-medication replacement, the replacement needs the police report number, recorded exactly as the patient gives it.

(4) A replacement is never authorized for controlled prescriptions.

(5) Damaged or spilled medication is treated as lost.

**How the terms combine (hypothetical cases).**

| Situation | Outcome under these terms |
|---|---|
| Standard Maintenance Prescription, tablets lost, no replacement in the past 12 months | one replacement fill may be authorized |
| Same prescription, one replacement already authorized 5 months ago | not below the cap of the class: no replacement under term (1) |
| Specialty Medication Prescription, medication stolen, patient gives a police report number | the number is recorded exactly as given |
| Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription, medication lost | never replaced (term 4) |
| Monitored Maintenance Prescription, a bottle spilled | treated as lost |
